articles.title: Kentucky appeals court dissolves injunction that granted 38 players, including Thomas Castellanos, Seth Trimble and Mark Mitchell, a fifth year of eligibility
articles.summary: The ruling further exemplifies the chaos surrounding the NCAA's five-for-five implementation.
articles.body:
Could quarterback Thomas Castellanos' time at Texas Tech already be over?

On Friday, the Kentucky Court of Appeals ruled against athletes from the class of 2022 who had been granted a fifth year of eligibility via a temporary injunction. According to On3 , a hearing is scheduled in the matter for Oct. 9 as the lawsuit is still pending.

Castellanos was part of a group of players who had successfully been granted a fifth season of eligibility in the 2026-27 school year in Kentucky. And while players have had their state court efforts upheld — or at least not yet overturned — the players who filed suit in Kentucky are now ineligible. No. 12 Texas Tech plays at Colorado on Saturday.

Friday's ruling is another sign of how haphazard and chaotic the NCAA's attempted implementation of its five-for-five rule has been. Over the summer, the NCAA announced that all players would have five school years to play five seasons starting with the 2026-27 athletic seasons. However, players who had played their fourth season in four school years in 2025-26 were not given a fifth year of eligibility.

The August suit involved 38 players, including former North Carolina basketball player Seth Trimble and former Missouri basketball player Mark Mitchell, along with Castellanos. Mitchell and Trimble, too, are ineligible. But their seasons haven't started yet. Mitchell was set to go to Kentucky before returning to Missouri. Trimble transferred to Louisville.

Kentucky linebacker Alex Afari is also among the players who are suddenly ineligible. Afari has 11 tackles through four games so far this season.

Castellanos was a late addition to Texas Tech's roster and has appeared in four games for the Red Raiders and attempted four passes as a backup to Will Hammond that went for 35 yards and two touchdowns in special play packages. He also threw an interception on the opening play of the Red Raiders' Week 3 win over Houston. He has rushed 10 times for 44 yards and two scores.

Before joining Texas Tech, Castellanos spent his freshman season at UCF. He played five games for the Knights before transferring to Boston College. He was the Eagles' starting QB in 2023 and for the start of the 2024 season before he was moved to the bench. He transferred to Florida State in 2025, where he was the Seminoles' starter and threw for over 2,700 yards, rushed for over 550 yards and had 24 total touchdowns.

articles.title: Man City guilty charges: Which clubs did 'inflated' money flow to in transfer market?
articles.summary: BBC Sport follows the trail of transfer money flowing to other clubs during Manchester City's period of financial rule-breaking.
articles.body:
The money flowed around football. It made a lot of other clubs richer. It helped teams everywhere and especially in the Premier League.

These have been some of the arguments used by those backing Manchester City in the media and online since the verdicts declaring the club guilty came in and an appeal was announced. The suggestion is that there was a net benefit to the game as a whole, and in particular the clubs to whom Manchester City paid big transfer fees.

The more than £900m by which the independent commission found the club had "inflated" its accounts was not all spent on transfer fees.

Clubs have many bills, including wages for players and other staff, utilities, insurance, infrastructure costs, commercial fees and much more.

But the roughly £1.2bn Man City spent on players between 2009-2018 (about £900m net spend) was more than anybody else in that period.

That outlay was vital in making them England's most successful club, and would surely have been heavily reduced had they not knowingly broken the rules, as the independent commission concluded.

So where did City's money flow to in the transfer market, and what impact did it have?

Man City confirm appeal against guilty verdict

Man City whistleblower to lose witness protection

Who did Man City pay most money to between 2009 and 2018?

The amount required to sign the player is the most obvious, but there are also agents fees, legal expenses, administration money and potentially signing-on bonuses.

That means the money dished out by Manchester City during the 'asterisk era' will have reached people and bodies who work in the background of football deal-making and is difficult to track.

But what can be done is analysis of the fundamental interactions between City and other clubs.

Below is a list of every club to whom Manchester City paid transfer fees between summer 2009 and winter 2018, in descending order from the most money to the least.

The list is for senior players and does not include free transfers, loans or academy graduates.

That is 46 different clubs in 19 national league systems.

For some of them, the fees paid by City were the highest the clubs had ever received at the time.

Looking at the spread of money among clubs demonstrates just how far and wide Manchester City 's money was spent.

The split in money spent on transfer fees by City during the timeframe is relatively even across some of the highest-ranked leagues in Europe, though the Premier League is higher than any other.

Just over a quarter of their total transfer outlay was paid to clubs in the English top flight.

They signed players from eight Premier League clubs, and the same amount in La Liga.

A combined £13m was spent on two players in the Championship.

Manchester City 's spending power unquestionably changed the world football transfer market - their willingness to pay higher fees and wages meant prices rose for everybody else too.

And once the world knows that a club has a wedge of cash burning a hole in its pocket courtesy of City, it can be difficult to spend it.

Asking prices may rise, and having an influx of money is no guarantee of it being well spent.

For many of the teams to whom City paid the most during this time, the money did not work out particularly beneficially.

Let's take a look at some of the more interesting cases.

First up, Wolfsburg. They immediately signed winger Julian Draxler for about half the fee received for Kevin de Bruyne in 2016, as well as others including veteran defender Dante.

Having lost De Bruyne, they dropped from second to eighth in the Bundesliga before narrowly avoiding relegation in the subsequent two seasons.

And things did not go particularly well for second highest-ranked club Monaco either.

The most direct replacements they signed following the sales of Benjamin Mendy and Bernardo Silva in the same summer to Manchester City - Terence Kongolo and Keita Balde - did not work out in the long run, and the team went from winning Ligue 1 and reaching the Champions League semi-finals to almost being relegated within two years.

The club City purchased most players from in the 2009-18 period - Arsenal (four) - did not mount a serious Premier League title challenge during that time.

Some clubs who did not receive payments from City could also argue that the spending of money from their "inflated" accounts compromised their chances.

For example, Manchester City paid very similar totals to Benfica and Porto during the era, but nothing to Sporting, the club which makes up the big three in Portugal.

Sporting did not win a title between 2009 and 2018. There are many reasons for that, but could one of them be the fact that their direct rivals received money from City that would perhaps not have been on offer had they followed football's financial rules?

What does Man City guilty verdict mean for their squad?

HMRC urged to scrutinise tax implications of Man City case

Man City not 'above the rules', says No 10 after backlash to Burnham remarks

There are also some ancillary fees which reached clubs whom Manchester City did not deal with directly.

Some players were subject to sell-on clauses, where the club City where buying the player from owed money to the previous team who owned the player.

For example, Queens Park Rangers earned roughly £9m from Raheem Sterling's move to City from Liverpool in 2015.

Barnsley took about £7m of the transfer fee paid to Everton for John Stones in 2016, and the Toffees also had to pass on about £2.5m to Wolves when Joleon Lescott moved to Manchester in 2009.

The Sterling and Stones clauses were worth more than most players operating in the English Football League at that time, significantly strengthening the financial positions of QPR and Barnsley.

To this day Barnsley have not sold a player for a higher amount than the fee they are believed to have received for Stones.

But QPR have not returned to the Premier League and Barnsley dropped down to League One from the Championship after two seasons.

Manchester City 's spending during the time in which they were breaking the rules certainly had an enormous impact, on their own upward trajectory, the futures of other clubs around the world and the wider football economy.

But the reality is that it is impossible to unweave the tapestry of football history during that time and since - too much has happened and there are too many indirect consequences.

The effects of that spending will reverberate for years to come.

articles.title: Tyler Adams Named USMNT Captain by Mauricio Pochettino After Tim Ream's International Retirement
articles.summary: United States men's national soccer team head coach Mauricio Pochettino has named midfielder Tyler Adams as the new captain after ex-captain and center back Tim Ream announced his international retirement.
articles.body:
United States men's national soccer team head coach Mauricio Pochettino has named midfielder Tyler Adams as the new captain after ex-captain and center back Tim Ream announced his international retirement .

The 27-year-old Adams, who also plays for Bournemouth, has made 60 lifetime appearances for the United States dating back to 2017.

Adams previously captained the United States squad at the 2022 FIFA World Cup, leading the Americans out of the group stage and into the Round of 16. Last May, Pochettino announced Ream as the team's captain for this year's World Cup. The Americans won their group and beat Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Round of 32 before losing to Belgium.

At the club level, Adams began his career with New York Red Bulls before moving to RB Leipzig in 2019. He left there in 2022 for a season with Leeds United before signing a five-year deal with Bournemouth in 2023. Adams helped the team finish sixth in the Premier League table last year.

Currently, the USMNT is playing a run of international friendlies. They recently beat Peru 4-1 and Chile 4-2 and will now face Mexico on Saturday and Canada on Tuesday.

articles.title: USMNT Readies for Duel in the Desert vs. Mexico

articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. – There are a lot of things to say about U.S. versus Mexico, a classic series that dates back more than 90 years since the first all-time meeting in 1934, but one point that players on the U.S. Men's National Team are conveying right now is that they expect the latest edition to live up to the rivalry tag.

"Dislike, hate. I mean, it's a rivalry," midfielder Tyler Adams said. "However, you want to describe a rivalry. When you talk about rivalries, whether it's in Europe in club football or whatever it is, there is a sense of always wanting to win and compete at the highest level. This is one of those games. It's gone on for a long time. There's a lot of history there, and history creates that rivalry, of course, but you just want that winning advantage. Anything you can do to win."

"Mexico is the biggest game for us," midfielder Gio Reyna said. "It's been circled on this window more than any game."

The USMNT meets Mexico for the 80th time on Saturday, Oct. 3 in Glendale, Ariz. The "Duel in the Desert" kicks off at 7:00 p.m. MT at State Farm Stadium, which is home to the NFL's Arizona Cardinals and can expand to seat approximately 73,000.

"It's going to be like a little war on the field," wingback Sergiño Dest said. "These are the toughest games, and you will feel it. The atmosphere is going to be amazing."

Saturday's matchup is the first time the two 2026 FIFA World Cup co-hosts have faced each other since last summer in the Concacaf Gold Cup Final. A young and relatively inexperienced U.S. side under Mauricio Pochettino in his first year as head coach fought bravely but fell short 2-1 at NRG Stadium in Houston as Mexico secured back-to-back Gold Cup titles.

The atmosphere for that Final was deemed World Cup-level, and with the October matchup hosted at an NFL stadium of a comparable capacity, the environment is expected to be just as loud and passionate.

"These games, I feel like it's the real culture and the real passion of football," Dest said. "Rivalries between teams in general are always amazing to see… playing with America against Mexico is one of the best games here. It's going to be a tough game."

"Ever since I first played against Mexico, it's always been the same," fullback Antonee Robinson said. "It doesn't matter whether it's a qualifier, an international match, Nations League, Gold Cup – it's always a fierce competition. You want to win, and it feels really personal."

Six players on Pochettino's current roster saw the field for that Gold Cup Final last summer, including the lone goal scorer for the USMNT that day, center back Chris Richards, and the man who assisted him, midfielder Sebastian Berhalter. The pair plus 11 more holdovers from the USMNT that won Group D to advance to the knockout stage of this summer's World Cup have been telling the 13 first-time call-ups in fall camp what to expect with a rivalry match in front of them.

"That it's never friendly and that it's going to be a fun game," Berhalter on what he told the younger players about Mexico. "It's great for them to see that and hopefully compete and add because we need them. It's going to be a great game."

"I'd rather you go into a tackle and run everywhere and get around the ball and be feisty and have a little tenacity to your game than sit back and watch the game go by," Adams said. "So, all these players that have the opportunity to play tomorrow, that's what we need from them."

For players like 18-year-old forward Julian Hall, who made program history by becoming the youngest player to score a goal in each of his two caps, it's an opportunity to see the rivalry for the first time up close and in person.

"I'm expecting a dogfight," Hall said. "I've watched a lot of them in the past, and I'm excited to see what it's like – the environment, the experience. Hopefully, we come out with a win."

The U.S. will be looking to extend its winning record over Mexico since 2021. The U.S. holds a 5W-2L-2D advantage in the series, including victories in the 2021 and 2024 editions of the Concacaf Nations League Finals as well as the 2021 Gold Cup championship match.

In the latest edition, the U.S. will also aim to continue its current run of form in a new era under Pochettino, which has gotten off to a winning start. The group is coming off back-to-back wins over Peru in Orlando, Fla. on Sept. 26 and Chile in St. Louis, Mo. on Sept. 29 to kick off the four-match fall window. So far, the team has scored four goals in each victory with a variety of contributions from players all over the pitch.

Like the U.S., Mexico is coming off a Round of 16 appearance in FIFA World Cup 2026. After winning Group A without conceding a goal, Mexico's run came to an end in a classic match against tournament semifinalist England at Estadio Azteca.

Since then, Mexico has introduced a new head coach, Rafael Márquez, to succeed the retired Javier Aguirre. One of the most legendary defenders in Mexican soccer history, Márquez is a five-time World Cup participant. His playing resume is stacked with trophies, including four La Liga titles. In 2006 as a member of FC Barcelona, he became the first Mexican player to win the UEFA Champions League. He, like Pochettino, has been signed with his Federation through 2030.

Upon his arrival, Márquez vowed to take Mexico "to another level." Two matches into his debut as manager, Mexico is unbeaten but still looking for its first win after a pair of 1-1 draws against Peru and Colombia in September.

Since the previous meeting last summer between the two senior National Teams, the two countries also met for a youth-level championship. Mexico defeated the U-19 U.S. Men's National Team to capture the 2026 Concacaf U-20 Men's Championship at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City on Aug. 9, 2026, Mexico's second consecutive title.

"Mexico, in the last year, went in a great direction," Reyna said. "A lot of good, young players coming through as well. So, it's not the easiest game."

For some of the younger players on the USMNT roster, there may be some nerves heading into Saturday's match. Hosting a rival in front of a large crowd is an intense atmosphere, but the message that veterans are delivering to these players has been clear: we are going to need you.

"We need that courage. We need that bravery. We need them to be fearless like they are, so that they can have an impact," Adams said.

"The only thing I can help them with is to stay calm and believe in all the abilities they trained for all these years and show what you got because that's what we need," Dest said.

Dest knows well what it's like to play in USA-Mexico matches in the desert. The wingback started the Concacaf Nations League Semifinal match between the two sides in 2023 at Allegiant Stadium. On a dominant night for the U.S., Dest assisted the third goal of the night to striker Ricardo Pepi as the U.S. defeated Mexico 3-0, giving the 25-year-old both respect for a tough opponent and a taste of what it takes to defeat a longstanding rival.

"Mexico is always going to be a tough opponent," Dest said. "They're always aggressive, and they want to win. And so do we. So it's going to be a difficult game for both sides, and may the best win."

articles.title: Report: Bears Decide on Starting QB vs. Jets
articles.summary: Tyson Bagent is reportedly expected to start for the Chicago Bears against the Jets despite Ben Johnson refusing to announce his quarterback.
articles.body:
Ben Johnson isn't saying who will start at quarterback for the Chicago Bears on Sunday, but it appears his secret may already be out.

NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport reported Friday evening that Tyson Bagent is expected to start against the New York Jets after receiving first-team practice reps throughout the week. Johnson, meanwhile, is refusing to publicly confirm Bagent over veteran Case Keenum, who just led Chicago to an impressive Monday Night Football victory over Philadelphia.

Chicago officially ruled Caleb Williams out Friday as he continues recovering from a hamstring injury, guaranteeing that either Bagent or Keenum will make the start. The Bears confirmed Williams will miss his second consecutive game , but Johnson wasn't interested in giving former Lions defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn any additional information.

That mystery apparently isn't quite as mysterious behind closed doors. Bagent has received the majority of the first-team work this week, and Rapoport now reports that the 26-year-old is expected to get the assignment against New York.

Ben Johnson Could Turn Away From the Hot Hand

The interesting part is what that decision would mean for Keenum.

The 38-year-old stepped in Monday night and helped Chicago beat the previously undefeated Eagles 27-7 , throwing for 247 yards and two touchdowns while adding another score on the ground. Keenum's performance gave Johnson a legitimate decision after Bagent had been working his way back from a concussion.

Bagent cleared concussion protocol before Monday's game but served as Keenum's backup against Philadelphia. He entered the season as Williams' primary backup after signing a two-year, $10 million extension in 2025, making a return to the starting lineup logical now that he's healthy.

Aaron Glenn Will Have to Prepare for Both

Johnson's refusal to announce his quarterback also creates an interesting subplot because the opposing head coach knows him extremely well.

Glenn and Johnson spent four seasons together on Dan Campbell's Lions staff before both departed Detroit for head-coaching jobs. Johnson now gets an opportunity to make his former colleague prepare for multiple quarterbacks, even if the growing expectation is that Bagent will ultimately get the football.

The Bears enter Sunday's game at 2-1 , while the Jets are coming off a 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Chicago has already won once without Williams, and now Johnson appears prepared to see if Bagent can make it two.

Rapoport apparently just did it for him.

articles.title: Tyler Adams begins second stint as USMNT captain ahead of Mexico rivalry match
articles.summary: The armband has returned to Tyler Adams, but the 27-year-old says it won’t change how he leads the USMNT: “I’m going to be the exact same person.”
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. — Whether or not he wears the captain's armband, Tyler Adams, through leadership and example, has always been a natural-born leader of the U.S. soccer team.

On Friday, though, Mauricio Pochettino put an official stamp on the 27-year-old midfielder's role, naming him captain for the 2030 World Cup cycle.

It's a reprise role for Adams, who, at age 23, captained the 2022 World Cup squad in Qatar and, in perhaps his finest moment, answered politically charged questions with eloquence and maturity the day before the U.S. match against Iran.

Center back Tim Ream was Pochettino's captain at this summer's World Cup. With Ream retiring from the international arena, Pochettino made a point at the start of this training camp — the first since the World Cup — to name a captain midway through the four-game schedule.

Adams captained the team in last Saturday's 4-1 win over Peru in Orlando and wing back Antonee Robinson did the honors in Tuesday's 4-2 victory over Chile in St. Louis.

On Friday, at a news conference previewing Saturday's showdown with rival Mexico at State Farm Stadium in nearby Glendale, Pochettino announced Adams' appointment.

"He's a perfect role model for everyone in the way that he can translate the philosophy, the culture, and represent this amazing country," Pochettino said. "He is the player and the person that can lead that period that we have ahead."

Pochettino consulted with his staff — but not the players — and informed the U.S. Soccer Federation's board of directors about his decision before telling the players ahead of Thursday's training session.

"Tyler is the perfect person first, and player and professional to be the leader in the way that we expect," Pochettino said. He added that he spoke with Adams throughout camp and "he knows exactly what we expect from him. He needs to challenge us, of course, the coaching staff."

Adams, in his third season with Bournemouth in the Premier League, has been a mainstay for the national team since 2021 under previous coach Gregg Berhalter.

"Getting the armband doesn't mean anything to me in being a leader or being different from who I am," he said. "I'm going to be the exact same person. I'm going to try and obviously lead this group into a winning culture and continuing to build what we're trying to build here. I want to represent my teammates in the best way possible. I want to represent the country in the best way possible, of course. This is just kind of the icing on top, cherry on top. We have a lot of work to do still but we're getting there."

Center back Chris Richards was also widely seen as a potential captain because of his leadership qualities, positive energy and relationships with the coaches and players.

Reflecting on his first tenure as captain, Adams said, "In 2022, obviously we were a very young team — one of the youngest at the World Cup. And although I was ready for that role, at the same time I've had the ability to grow both on and off the field in the period now leading up to this past World Cup."

He said he has learned from Ream and others who wore the armband during the last World Cup cycle.

His first match of this term is one that, with a roster peppered with international novices, will require the utmost direction and temperament. Meetings with Mexico are the most impassioned on the U.S. calendar, often replete with the dark arts and confrontations.

With most of the crowd expected to support Mexico, the U.S. is bracing for what amounts to an away game.

"One-nil down for us," a smiling Pochettino said of El Tri's "home-field" advantage.

Pochettino said he will use a similar lineup to the prior two matches, starting experienced and inexperienced players. Twelve U.S. players have made their senior debuts in this camp, with some playing pivotal roles in the impressive victories against South American competition.

In choosing his lineups, Pochettino has taken into consideration workloads for players balancing club and country.

"We need to be responsible with the players and also with the clubs," he said. "It's a very difficult window with four games, a lot of travel, long distance. That is what I want to translate to the clubs. I think that we are caring about the player."

The U.S. will also play Canada on Tuesday in St. Paul before the players return to their clubs.

"What I expect is the same intensity that the team showed against Peru and Chile," Pochettino said. "It's not going to change. The message from the beginning was enjoy, give your best and to play not because of the opponent but because of ourselves. We will defend our shirt. They are so smart, so intelligent – the whole team and the whole group."

Adams has been a part of many U.S.-Mexico rumbles.

"Dislike, hate — I mean, it's a rivalry," he said. "However, you want to describe a rivalry. When you talk about rivalries, whether it's in Europe in club football or whatever it is, there is a sense of just always wanting to win and compete at the highest level. This is one of those games."

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Revealed as College GameDay Guest Picker for OSU-Iowa After Fever's WNBA Playoff Exit
articles.summary: Indiana Fever star guard (and former Iowa Hawkeye) Caitlin Clark will be College GameDay's guest picker on Saturday when ESPN's college football pregame show rolls into Iowa City for No. 14 Iowa's home game against No. 5 Ohio State.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star guard (and former Iowa Hawkeye) Caitlin Clark will be College GameDay's guest picker on Saturday when ESPN's college football pregame show rolls into Iowa City for No. 14 Iowa's home game against No. 5 Ohio State.

Clark, of course, became a superstar at Iowa, leading the Hawkeyes to back-to-back national championship game appearances. She is a three-time first-team Associated Press All-American (2022–2024) and a two-time consensus national player of the year (2023-2024).

Clark also left town with a host of records. Of note, she's the all-time Division I scoring leader (men or women) with 3,951 points.

She just finished her third season with the Fever, who went 28-16 but fell short in the first round of the playoffs to the Las Vegas Aces, the defending WNBA champions. Clark had her best season as a pro, averaging 22.3 points (third in the WNBA) and 8.3 assists (second).

College GameDay is in Iowa City for the first time since 2006, when Iowa hosted Ohio State, then the No. 1 team in the nation. OSU won that game, 38-17, but Iowa is obviously hoping for a different result.

The 4-0 Hawkeyes enter this game after defeating Michigan on the road, 20-19, with a game-ending 16-yard touchdown from quarterback Hank Brown to wide receiver Reece Vander Zee.

So ESPN is in town for a big one. Clark (and the rest of the GameDay crew) will be making their picks just before the show closes at noon ET. Kickoff at Kinnick Stadium is set for 3:30 p.m.

articles.summary: Northwestern's new Ryan Field made its debut for a matchup with Penn State on Friday night.
articles.body:
Northwestern's new Ryan Field made its debut for a matchup with Penn State on Friday night.

The Wildcats' $875 million stadium was showcased in several videos and photos posted on social media.

The Wildcats played their first two games of the 2026 season at Northwestern Medicine Field at Martin Stadium before switching to the new 35,000-seat venue for Friday's contest.

The updated stadium itself is 320,000 square feet larger than the old Ryan Field and is surrounded by 200,000 square feet of festival grounds .

Northwestern football head coach David Braun was impressed with the seating design of the stadium.

"The fans are truly on top of the action. I mean they are a part of the game," Braun said, per NBC 5 Chicago . "Standing at midfield, I mean you almost feel like you can reach out and touch the stands. And the acoustics that that's going to create with the canopy creates for an incredible opportunity for a home-field advantage."

The Wildcats own a 2-1 record this season, looking to build upon their 7-6 finish during their 2025 campaign.

articles.title: 'Have good memories of India, I’m happy to be back': Vinicius Jr returns to India 10 years after BRICS Cup breakthrough
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Vinicius Jr sported the biggest smile as Brazil stepped inside the team hotel, after a 11-hour flight from Brisbane late on Friday.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Vinicius Jr sported the biggest smile as Brazil stepped inside the team hotel, after a 11-hour flight from Brisbane late on Friday. The star winger happily posed for pictures and signed autographs. India surely brings happy memories to Vinicius’ mind.Ten years ago, Vinicius was part of Brazil’s U-16 squad at the BRICS Cup in Goa. He did not make the brightest of starts. In fact, he wasn’t even starting games, until he proved himself with goals against Russia and India as a second-half substitute.At the end of it all, Vinicius emerged as the standout player for Brazil, scoring five goals to scoop the top scorer award. “These are good memories because I came here when I was a boy,” Vinicius said in an interview with CBF TV. “I didn't know I would come back here, and I didn't know that even back then the (Indian) fans already had a great affection for me, because I came to this competition and then the (U-17) World Cup happened and I couldn't come. Everyone from India sent me messages, it's an audience that follows me closely, loves football, loves Brazil and I'm happy to be back here.”When Vinicius came to Goa for BRICS Cup, not many had heard of him. A few months later, he was the best performer at the South American Under-17 Championship, finishing as the leading goalscorer with seven goals. Soon, Real Madrid knocked on Flamengo’s doors and came up with a record offer for the teenager. On Saturday at Salt Lake stadium, Vinicius will wear Brazil colours again in India. “It will be a great day for India and for us too. articles.title: España regenta el mundo
articles.standfirst: La campeona del mundo domina con autoridad los duelos entre campeonas del mundo y de Europa desde la llegada de De la Fuente
articles.summary: La campeona del mundo domina con autoridad los duelos entre campeonas del mundo y de Europa desde la llegada de De la Fuente
articles.body: Oviedo está lista. La selección española regresa a la capital del Principado más de una década después. En septiembre de 2015, el Carlos Tartiere vio ganar a su selección por 2-0 camino de la Euro de Francia. Con Del Bosque a los mandos, aquella era una selección con una sola estrella en la camiseta y que trataba de resistir al paso del tiempo y a éxitos de los que ya se hablaba en pasado. La España que llega a la casa del Oviedo es un equipo capaz ya de mirar a la cara a aquel que dominó el mundo. Como aquella selección, esta es a la vez campeona de Europa y del mundo. Además, en el palmarés de esta generación está también la Liga de las Naciones y hay cuatro campeones olímpicos. España luce como dueña y señora del fútbol mundial. Su camiseta exhibe los parches que la hacen señora del mundo y de Europa. No hace falta mucho más, pero si alguien duda de que España es la número uno basta con que repase los partidos entre las mejores selecciones desde que llegó De la Fuente en marzo de 2023. Si se cruzan los resultados entre selecciones campeonas del mundo, la España de De la Fuente es la que más partidos ha jugado: once. Solo ha dejado de ganar uno. Fue el amistoso ante Brasil en el Bernabéu, en marzo de 2024, empatado por la pentacampeona mundial con un penalti en el minuto 97. El resto han sido victorias españolas. Dos en finales: a Argentina en la del Mundial y a Inglaterra en la Euro. Hasta tres veces ha ganado España a la Francia que, torneo tras torneo, aparece como gran favorita, cargada de poderes y que tiene en la selección española a su kriptonita. Francia es la segunda de las ocho campeonas del mundo que más se han enfrentado a sus homólogas. Pero su balance nada tiene que ver con el demoledor español: cuatro victorias y seis derrotas, la mitad de ellas sufridas ante sus vecinos del sur. España ha ganado en Wembley, levantando el partido, y derrotado a Alemania en los cuartos de la Euro en suelo germano. Si ese experimento se traslada a las ganadoras de la Eurocopa, incluyendo a Inglaterra, que nunca la ganó, pero estuvo en las dos últimas finales, el resultado de la prueba es el mismo. Nadie ha ganado más que España y ninguna de las selecciones campeonas de Europa presenta un cero en su casillero de derrotas en el periodo que va de marzo de 2023 hasta hoy. En esa ruta, España ha derrotado a todas las reinas de Europa con las que ha jugado menos a una. Con los holandeses ha jugado dos veces, en los cuartos de final de la pasada Liga de las Naciones: 2-2 en Rotterdam y 3-3 en Mestalla. Pero fue España la que accedió, a través de la tanda de penaltis, a la Final Four. En ese contundente dominio ante las mejores selecciones del planeta se sustentan esas dos rachas nunca conocidas hasta ahora en la historia del fútbol: los 40 partidos consecutivos sin derrota, que se elevan a 41 cuando se cuentan solo los oficiales. El regreso del Mundial no ha hecho que España se contente con lo hecho. Lo demostró ante Inglaterra. Con Oviedo preparada para prolongar la fiesta que se vivió en Sevilla y tenga continuación en el Carlos Tartiere, el partido tiene una alta carga simbólica. En el banquillo de la República Checa están Santi Denia y Pablo Amo. Son dos entrenadores estrechamente vinculados a Luis de la Fuente y a la formación de la mayoría de los jugadores que van a ser sus rivales esta noche. Con los dos entrenadores contrarios al formato de cuatro partidos en esta primera ventana, las rotaciones están aseguradas. España parte desde la comodidad de jugar en casa con dos victorias en sus dos primeros partidos. Y la seguridad de que ponga a quien ponga De la Fuente los cambios no van a afectar al organismo del equipo. Los checos aparecen con dos derrotas en un proceso de cambio que mira a más largo plazo. Y con bajas importantes respecto al equipo que estuvo en el Mundial. La noche ovetense tiene pinta de fiesta española. Pero la regenta no se fía de nadie en Vetusta, la ciudad que inmortlizó Clarín, de Ana Ozores. De La Regenta.

articles.title: Coufal, el último checoslovaco
articles.standfirst: Es el único jugador del equipo de Santi Denia nacido antes de la separación de Checoslovaquia
articles.summary: Es el único jugador del equipo de Santi Denia nacido antes de la separación de Checoslovaquia
articles.body: Vladimir Coufal es el jugador más veterano de la República Checa. Tiene 34 años y nació el 22 de agosto de 1992 en Ludgerovice. En la fecha de su nacimiento aún existía Checoslovaquia. Era un país con fecha de caducidad. Fue un verano de alta intensidad política para dar forma legal a lo que casi todos estaban de acuerdo: la separación de checos y eslovacos. Eso ocurrió el 31 de diciembre: la República Federal Checa y Eslovaca dejó de existir; la República Checa y Eslovaquia se convirtieron en sus estados sucesores. De todos los jugadores convocados por Santi Denia en su primera lista como seleccionador checo, Coufal es el único que nació antes de que Checoslovaquia dejase de existir. En su casa creció con historias de lo que fue el deporte checoslovaco durante los años del Telón de Acero. Su madre, Alena Drevjaná, representó a su país en los Juegos Olímpicos de 1988. A Seúl viajó como integrante del equipo de gimnasia rítmica. Checoslovaquia acabó séptima por equipos y Alena ocupó la vigesimosexta plaza de una clasificación que dominó la soviética Yelena Shushunova. Si no fue olímpica cuatro años antes en Los Ángeles fue por el boicot de los países comunistas. De esa renuncia nacieron los Juegos de la Amistad en su país, Olomouc. Allí fue bronce por equipos y en barra. Lo que fue su madre en la élite de la gimnasia checoslovaca lo heredó Vladimir en el fútbol. Creció en la cantera del Banik Ostrava. Dio pasos que lo condujeron a uno de los grandes del fútbol checo, el Slavia. Las puertas de la selección se le abrieron en noviembre de 2017, en un amistoso contra Qatar en Doha. La cuenta de partidos del lateral derecho checo con su país está en 62. Si no está en alguno más es porque en noviembre de 2023, en Moldavia, fue expulsado de la concentración del equipo. Fue la respuesta de la Federación a que él, Jakub Brabec y Jan Kuchta fueran sorprendidos saliendo de fiesta dos días antes del partido. Regresó a Praga y no fue convocado para los partidos de marzo. Pero fue perdonado y estuvo en la Euro. Como este verano en el Mundial. Vladimir, que este verano dejó el West Ham tras cinco años para recalar en el Hoffenheim, tiene dos hermanos que son estrellas del patinaje artístico de su país: Petr y Jana. Rival de España en el doble duelo de la Nations de 2023, para este partido es uno de los problemas de Santi Denia. Ante Croacia sufrió un problema de rodilla que le hizo ser baja contra Inglaterra.

articles.title: Fresneda y los Denia
articles.standfirst: El lateral, que puede debutar ante los checos, tuvo a Santi como entrenador y a Marcos como compañero en las inferiores de la selección
articles.summary: El lateral, que puede debutar ante los checos, tuvo a Santi como entrenador y a Marcos como compañero en las inferiores de la selección
articles.body: Iván Fresneda se quedó en la grada en el partido de Wembley. En el Sánchez-Pizjuán estuvo entre los 23 que se vistieron. Calentó, pero no llegó a debutar. Esta noche puede llegar el momento en el que se estrene con la absoluta. Marc Pubill es uno de los cuatro jugadores de la selección que no se han perdido un minuto de los 180 jugados. Los otros son Unai Simón, Cubarsí y Cucurella. La rotación apunta a ellos. Si el duelo contra los checos es el primero de Fresneda con España será ante un rival que tiene como entrenador a Santi Denia y segundo a Pablo Amo. Los dos aparecen en su paso por las inferiores. Denia lo tuvo en la sub 19. Fue un escalón antes, en la sub 18, donde Fresneda dio sus primeros pasos en la selección. El 28 de abril de 2022, la sub 18 española se enfrentó a la sub 20 de Marruecos en el Stade Prince Moulay Hassan de Rabat. Pablo Amo formó un equipo en el que Fresneda era el lateral derecho y que ganó 0-2 con goles de Jon Julen Guerrero y Andrés Caro. El delantero centro de aquel once cierra el cuadrado del que forman parte Fresneda, Pablo Amo y Santi Denia. Porque el 9 de España fue Marcos Denia, el hijo de Santi. Formado en la cantera del Atlético de Madrid, Marcos, 22 años, es hoy el delantero centro del primer filial del Getafe. De aquel equipo de Pablo Amo, Fresneda está a un paso de ser el segundo en debutar con la absoluta y el primero en partido oficial. El central diestro era Cristhian Mosquera. El zaguero del Arsenal jugó los dos amistosos de marzo. Y allí estaba Ilias Akhomach, que ya lleva 14 partidos con Marruecos.

articles.title: La vuelta de Robin
articles.standfirst: A pesar de llevar casi un año alejado de la selecció, Le Normand es el octavo jugador con más mimutos en la era De la Fuente
articles.summary: A pesar de llevar casi un año alejado de la selecció, Le Normand es el octavo jugador con más mimutos en la era De la Fuente
articles.body: Robin Le Normand no juega con al selección desde hace casi un año. El 10 de octubre estuvo en el 4-0 a Bulgaria en Valladolid. Jugó 71 minutos y un corte en el labio hizo que Vivian entrara en su lugar. Era un fijo para el Mundial, pero entre lesiones y pérdida de protagonismo en el Atlético de Madrid, sus acciones mundialistas se fuero devaluando. Hasta quedarse fuera ante el empuje de Eric García y Pubill. Ahora está de vuelta en la selección. La lesión de Eric en Wembley supuso su llamada. Le Normand siempre ha sido un jugador de confianza para De la Fuente, por más que se quedara sin Mundial.Lo explica que después de casi un año de ausencia siga dentro de los once jugadores con más minutos desde que el riojano es entrenador. Con 2.094 es el octavo. Antes de la lista del mundialista sabía que había perdido terreno. La decepción existió, pero echó mano de su fuerza menta, de su familia, de su gente cercana. Lo aprovechó para limpiar la mente, viajar mucho y lejos. Para dedica tiempo a la buena cantidad de hobbies que tiene al margen del fútbol. Y a entrenar. Porque tenía claro que debía llegar a su club preparado para recuperar el terreno cedido la pasada campaña. La llamada del domingo le cogió por sorpresa. No contaba con que la baja en el lateral derecho le afectara. Se sumó a la selección con el espíritu de siempre: el de sumar, juegue o no. De la Fuente sabe que Le Normand es uno de sus soldados, un jugador que siempre ha respondido en la selección a lo que se le ha pedido. Ante la República Checa, 354 días después, puede volver a jugar.

articles.title: España, Oviedo y el árbitro que inventó A Bola
articles.standfirst: España se estrenó en la capital de Asturias ante Yugoslavia y con arbitraje del portugués Joao Joaquim Tavares da Silva
articles.summary: España se estrenó en la capital de Asturias ante Yugoslavia y con arbitraje del portugués Joao Joaquim Tavares da Silva
articles.body: La selección española juega por sexta vez en Oviedo, una ciudad que no pisaba desde 2015. Lo hace más de 94 años después de su primera aparición en Vetusta. Fue el 24 de abril de 1932, bajo bandera republicana y con Yugoslavia como rival. Ese día se inauguró el campo de Buenavista. Se superó por mucho el límite de espectadores, unos 5.000 más de los 15.000 permitidos. Debutó con España un delantero de leyenda, Isidro Lángara. Jugaba en el Oviedo, marcó el primer gol de España y el primero de los 17 que hizo en sus 12 partidos con la selección. Es el único que tiene una media superior al gol por partido: 1,41. El árbitro elegido para ese duelo es un nombre perdido en el tiempo. Pero si se bucea en la biografía de Joao Joaquim Tavares da Silva se encuentra una vida fascinante unida al deporte y al periodismo. Nació el 29 de diciembre de 1903, en Estarreja. Su vida iba encaminada para ser abogado. Ingresó en la Facultad de Derecho de Lisboa antes de que el pasado siglo llegara a los años 30, pero no se licenció hasta 1952, cuando tenía como profesores a compañeros de aulas en sus primeras clases. No era mal estudiante; era un loco del deporte y del periodismo. A los libros les ganó la pelota. Tavares da Silva es una figura capital para entender el desarrollo del fútbol portugués. Comenzó a jugar en un club que hace mucho dejó de existir, el Portugal FC. Pero pronto viró hacia el mundo del arbitraje. Su figura y amor por el fútbol fueron más allá de Portugal. Se convirtió en árbitro internacional. El partido entre España y Yugoslavia en Oviedo fue el gran momento de su carrera. La pasión por el arbitraje le llevó a ser presidente del Colegio de Árbitros de Lisboa. Desempeñó una intensa labor en favor de su colectivo y en la mejora de las reglas del juego. Ese camino le condujo a entrar en la Federación Portuguesa. Fue directivo. Y mucho más. En la primavera de 1931 fue nombrado seleccionador nacional. Ese cargo lo iba a ocupar en cuatro etapas distintas. Se puso a los mandos de una selección marginal en el fútbol europeo, pero a la que poco a poco fue acercando a los mejores. Él fue quien logró que Portugal derrotara por primera vez a España: 4-1, el 26 de enero de 1947. Era el decimosexto duelo ibérico. Lo que en Portugal fue una gran fiesta, en España causó desazón y críticas feroces. Con Tavares en su banquillo, Portugal fue capaz al fin de ganar lejos de su país. Fue el 26 de mayo de 1947, en el que era el partido número 65 de la selección lusa. En Dublín, con goles de Jesus Correia y Araújo, Portugal ganó 0-2 para inaugurar su cuenta foránea. Suyo fue el mando en la primera vez que Portugal venció a Inglaterra: 3-1, en Oporto, en mayo de 1955. Fue una liberación para Tavares. Porque años antes, el 25 de mayo de 1947, él fue el primer seleccionador portugués en enfrentarse a los ingleses. Fue en Lisboa y el partido acabó 0-10. De esa paliza data el gol más rápido marcado por Inglaterra: Tommy Lawton, a los 17 segundos de juego. Tavares dimitió tras esa humillación. De todo lo que aportó Joao Tavares da Silva al deporte portugués, buena parte fue desde las páginas de los periódicos. Su firma fue habitual en las páginas deportivas de diferentes publicaciones, no sólo las diarias. Idea suya fue la revista semanal A Bola, que vivió entre 1932 y 1934. Años después, otro seleccionador portugués, Candido de Oliveira, recuperó el nombre para fundar el periódico que lleva el mismo nombre desde el 29 de enero de 1945. Además de sus artículos, su voz se hizo habitual en la radio y en las secciones deportivas de la naciente televisión. Tras superar una grave enfermedad, en septiembre de 1958, siendo redactor jefe del Diario de Lisboa, se empeñó en cubrir la Vuelta a Portugal. Ofreció un reportaje cubriendo una etapa en bicicleta. Tuvo que regresar de urgencia a Lisboa al sufrir una crisis. El 15 de septiembre fue operado. El 19 de octubre moría en su casa de Lisboa.

articles.title: El Rayo vuelve a Vallecas a lo grande
articles.standfirst: El cuadro franjirrojo debutará esta temporada en su feudo para disputar el Trofeo de Vallecas
articles.summary: El cuadro franjirrojo debutará esta temporada en su feudo para disputar el Trofeo de Vallecas
articles.body: El Rayo vuelve a su hogar. El Rayo regresará a su estadio esta temporada para jugar la trigésimo tercera edición del Trofeo de Vallecas. Una copa que se disputó por primera vez en el año 1970 y que después de siete años (la última que se jugó fue en el año 2019 frente al Alcorcón), se volverá a vivir en el barrio. El día 14, la Comunidad de Madrid levantó la suspensión de la sede franjirroja y ya es apta para acoger una actividad deportiva. El estadio lleva 'vacío' desde el 17 de mayo de 2026 cuando se jugó la última jornada como local de la temporada 25/26. Fue un día de despedidas. Vallecas se despidió de dos de sus héroes, como lo son Óscar Trejo e Iñigo Pérez, y de toda la plantilla antes del viaje más bonito de sus vidas. Desde entonces, todo lo que ha tenido que ver con el asunto del estadio ha acabado en tragedia. Cierre del estadio, enfrentamientos entre instituciones y una afición relegada al exilio. La vuelta a Vallecas será un día de bienvenidas. En ninguno de los encuentros que se han jugado en Butarque se ha llegado a los 5.000 espectadores y ahora se espera un estadio abarrotado que reciba a los 'héroes' de Leipzig, al nuevo entrenador, Beñat San José y demás caras nuevas de la plantilla. En estos momentos, "las instalaciones inspeccionadas se encuentran operativas y en condiciones adecuadas para su funcionamiento ordinario", según la segunda auditoría realizada. Sin embargo, el estadio aún cuenta con déficits que se deberán solucionar a lo largo de este mes por lo que el Rayo aún tiene trabajo por delante. El Cagliari será el rival del Rayo en este Trofeo de Vallecas que se disputará a las 14:00 horas. Ambos conjuntos ya se midieron en un encuentro amistoso en el año 2011 en el que el resultado fue favorable para los italianos.

articles.title: La India ofrece otra oportunidad a Endrick
articles.standfirst: El delantero apunta a titular en el tercer y último amistoso de Brasil en este parón
articles.summary: El delantero apunta a titular en el tercer y último amistoso de Brasil en este parón
articles.body: De Brisbane a Calcuta. La selección brasileña que dirige Carlo Ancelotti jugará este sábado (16.00 horas) en la India su tercer y último amistoso de este parón FIFA tras haber sumado empate y triunfo sobre Australia en un doble enfrentamiento previo. Será en el monumental estadio Yuva Bharati Krirangan, con capacidad para 120.000 espectadores. Una llegada, la de la pentacampeona Mundial, que ha supuesto un revuelo monumental en el país asiático. La selección brasileña solo ha tenido una sesión de entrenamiento en suelo indio y se espera que 'Carletto' ponga sobre el verde un equipo con cambios significativos respecto al que se impuso 2-4 a Australia... y del que salió tocado (y con avión de vuelta a Barcelona) un Raphinha que finalmente no tiene nada grave. "No es una prueba, es una oportunidad para demostrar la calidad que poseen. Así que deben tomarse todo esto con calma, porque no es una prueba para ellos", era el mensaje de Ancelotti a los menos habituales antes de un partido que, por ejemplo, verá debutar a Pedro Morisco, portero de Coritiba. "El partido puede salir bien o mal, pero no nos importa lo que hagamos en el futuro. Les daremos otras oportunidades", analizaba el italiano en su tercer amistoso al frente de la 'Canarinha' desde el debacle del Mundial 2026 contra Noruega. "Aquella derrota... este período difícil es para nosotros una motivación para crear una nueva generación de jugadores que puedan competir por los mejores en los próximos años", comentaba 'Carletto' al tiempo que elogiaba a Endrick (titular en el primer partido) en rueda de prensa. Tanto él como Vini Jr. deberían ser las referencias en ataque de Brasil en Calcuta. Si bien el extremo viene de marcar, el '9' no ha visto puerta en ninguno de los partidos previos pese a la confianza (y minutos) que le ha dado Ancelotti.

articles.title: Responsable de cantera... en Georgia
articles.standfirst: Agustín Vara, ex del Atlético como jugador y como técnico, dirige el programa de desarrollo del FC Rustavi • También ayuda al staff del primer equipo, un ascendido que pelea por el título
articles.summary: Agustín Vara, ex del Atlético como jugador y como técnico, dirige el programa de desarrollo del FC Rustavi • También ayuda al staff del primer equipo, un ascendido que pelea por el título
articles.body: "Tuve la oportunidad hace dos años ya a través de Tornike, un intermediario que vive en Ponferrada. Entonces pedí unas condiciones que no se dieron, pero el pasado 6 de agosto me volvió a llamar: ‘Vente, que tenemos que hablar’. Entonces me propuso este proyecto...” Este proyecto es el del FC Rustavi georgiano, que ha confiado en el español Agustín Vara (Pobladura del Valle, 1973) como director de su programa de desarrollo (léase responsable de sus categorías inferiores) y, de paso, como ayudante del segundo entrenador del primer equipo: “Estuvo en España 15 años, así que domina el idioma. Hablamos, le ayudo con algunos ejercicios, yo soy su mano derecha ahí y él es la mía con la Academia”. Porque, más allá de esa otra labor, Vara ha llegado sobre todo para liderar la creación e implementación de un sistema deportivo completamente nuevo y moderno, “donde cada jugador talentoso pueda desarrollarse”, cuyas claves explica el propio club: experiencia y metodología europeas (estándares de entrenamiento de academias líderes); scouting profesional; entrenamiento físico, táctico y mental adaptado a las características de la edad; alianza europea (estrecha cooperación con clubes extranjeros); programas internacionales (proyectos de intercambio y torneos) y un camino directo de la Academia hacia el fútbol profesional. La última experiencia de Vara en España pasó por el cuerpo técnico del Atlético B, ahora Madrileño, equipo en el que también se había desempeñado de corto décadas antes. Como futbolista pasó asimismo por Valladolid, Hércules, Universidad de Las Palmas o Xerez, como entrenador comenzó en la cantera del Leganés (llegando al primer equipo) antes de acabar en la entidad rojiblanca con los ‘staffs’ que fueron liderando Óscar Fernández, Nacho Fernández o Luis Tevenet. Y ahora, Georgia. Y ahora, Rustavi. Avalado por videos de antiguos compañeros o de jugadores que están ahora en Primera división. “Es un recién ascendido, pero durante buena parte de la temporada ha estado líder. Ahora faltan los últimos nueve partidos, porque la Liga acaba en diciembre, y estamos cuatro equipos en pocos puntos. También se ha llegado a semifinales de Copa, que es una posible vía para entrar en competiciones europeas”, explica Agustín durante la charla con MARCA, recordando que UEFA excluyó momentáneamente de las mismas al Dinamo Batumi, uno de los rivales directos, por problemas financieros. “Aquí comenzó a correrse la voz de que había llegado un español... y ahora yo creo que ya me conocen en todo el país”, bromea. “Hemos pasado de algo más de 200 chavales a casi 800. Me está costando ordenar todo esto y creo que algún otro entrenador me voy a traer. Las instalaciones son increíbles y técnicamente hay un gran nivel. Hay chavales en nuestro filial o en nuestro juvenil que podrían estar en las mejores canteras de España”. Por ahí surgen luego, y entre otros, los Kvaratskhelia o Mikautadze. La distancia entre Rustavi y Tiflis, la capital, no llega a los 30 kilómetros. “En España vivo en Móstoles, así que estoy acostumbrado...”, explica justo el día en el que se ha mudado por fin a un piso ofrecido por el club después de varias semanas de hotel: “Mi hijo mayor está jugando al fútbol con beca en Estados Unidos y el pequeño pertenece al Juvenil B del Getafe”. La escuadra de Pepe Bordalás, precisamente, jugará Conference en Georgia, contra el Iberia, el próximo 26 de noviembre: “Ya he quedado para ir a ver el partido... y el chaval ya me metió una sudadera azulona en la maleta”. Vara ha firmado por cinco años con sendas cláusulas, una para que pueda regresar a España si el proceso de adaptación no es satisfactorio, otra para que no lo reclame un rival del Rustavi: “Ellos me han traído y no van a dejar que me vaya después a uno de sus rivales. Es lógico”, completa desde la distancia.

articles.title: Llorente no duda: en Madrid... y seguir en el Atlético
articles.standfirst: El 14, que acaba contrato el próximo 30 de junio, sólo piensa en rojiblanco... y renovará
articles.summary: El 14, que acaba contrato el próximo 30 de junio, sólo piensa en rojiblanco... y renovará
articles.body: Es el tercer capitán. Encontró en el Atlético, pese a su pasado de blanco, su ecosistema en el mundo del fútbol. Referente, imprescindible, intocable. Cualquier adjetivo para explicar la importancia de Marcos Llorente en el conjunto del Metropolitano se antoja corto. El 14 representa como pocos los valores del club. Por su esfuerzo y su compromiso cada vez que luce la rojiblanca. Lo más importante, en su actual situación contractual acabando contrato el 30 de junio, es lo que piensa el campeón del Mundo. Y su pensamiento sólo admite seguir sí o sí en Madrid, ciudad en la que nació y en la que tiene todo lo que necesita en su tan ‘comentado’ estilo de vida. De ahí que por su cabeza no pase nada que no sea seguir muchos años más en un club el que acabará siendo el heredero del brazalete de Koke y Oblak. De ahí que pese a rumores (algunos más que infundados) la continuidad de Llorente en el Atlético no admite dudas. Su pensamiento es renovar y, quizá, poner fin a su carrera siendo una de las grandes leyendas de la historia del club. En ello está encaminado...

articles.title: El Espanyol se instala en una montaña rusa
articles.standfirst: Tras un arranque de temporada ilusionante, las últimas derrotas han hecho daño al equipo
articles.summary: Tras un arranque de temporada ilusionante, las últimas derrotas han hecho daño al equipo
articles.body: El inicio de temporada del Espanyol ha sido un tanto extraño, irregular y con ciertos altibajos tanto en los resultados como ene le juego del equipo que han hecho que el ambiente en este primer parón sea algo enrarecido. La temporada arrancó de forma ilusionante para la afición perica, con el primer proyecto de Monchi al frente de la parcela deportiva y con varios refuerzos interesantes que incrementaban el nivel de la plantilla. Además, los primeros resultados fueron positivos, con un gran inicio de temporada goleando al Levante o un buen partido – pese a la derrota en los instantes finales , ante el Real Madrid. Además, poco después se logró también la primera victoria a domicilio en Pamplona, con un Roberto Fernández estelar. A ello se sumaba la llegada de Bryan Zaragoza con la temporada ya iniciada, otra noticia positiva y que hacía soñar a la afición blanquiazul. Tras ello, los primeros contratiempos del curso que incluso –en algunos sectores– han hecho que se vuelva a poner en duda la figura de Manolo González en el banquillo perico. La derrota en Leganés ante el Rayo Vallecano hizo daño, ya que como el propio técnico dijo, la imagen del equipo en el primer tiempo fue extremadamente mala. Lo peor estaba por llegar. En el último encuentro antes del parón, derrota por 1-3 en el RCDE Stadium ante el Elche. Una derrota que ha haría mella y escocería mucho, ya que el conjunto ilicitano jugó más de 90 minutos con un futbolista menos. Ni disputando todo el encuentro con un hombre más, el Espanyol pudo poner en apuros a un Elche que fue superior y levantó los primeros pitos de la temporada en el RCDE Stadium. El Espanyol necesita mejorar y retomar el rumbo con el que arrancó la temporada y este parón seguro que le viene bien a su técnico para dar un giro al equipo. La explosión goleadora de Roberto Fernández, algo que le costó el curso pasado. El delantero está mostrando un acierto por encima de lo normal de cara a portería, convirtiendo cada una de las ocasiones de las que goza. Su sociedad con Javi Hernández, una de las grandes noticias de la temporada. Lo que están aportando los futbolistas que han regresado de cesión, como Javi Hernández, Hinojo o Marcos Fernández es otro de los aspectos a tener muy en cuenta. Los jóvenes han dado un paso al frente y han ganado pese en el equipo. La dinámica del Espanyol en los primeros partidos era de notable alto. Sin embargo, la dos últimas derrotas ante Rayo Vallecano y Elche le han hecho bajar la nota hasta un 5. La caída del equipo en las últimas jornadas, mostrando dificultades para generar en ataque incluso ante equipo con un futbolista menos. El Espanyol no pudo ganar en su estadio a un Elche que disputó todo el partido con 10 hombres, ni tampoco al Sevilla en el RCDE Stadium, que también jugó media hora con un futbolista menos. El equipo perico ha sido incapaz de ganar algunos partidos que se le han puesto muy de cara. Roberto Fernández, máximo goleador del equipo que pasa por su mejor momento, convocado por Luis de la Fuente con España. Javi Hernández también podría entrar en la terna, con un debut estelar del canterano que está firmando grandes números como asistente. El poco peso que han tenido algunos de los refuerzos que han llegado este verano, como Moscardo, Hartman, o Drkusic, que apenas han gozado de minutos en lo que va de curso.

articles.title: Sevilla: el sufrimiento va camino de desaparecer
articles.standfirst: El gran inicio de temporada del equipo de Luis García Plaza invita al optimismo
articles.summary: El gran inicio de temporada del equipo de Luis García Plaza invita al optimismo
articles.body: Después de otro final de temporada de apretar los dientes peleando por la permanencia en la máxima categoría, Luis García Plaza, que llegó en marzo sustituyendo a Matías Almeyda, diseñó una plantilla de la mano del director deportivo José Ignacio Navarro, que sustituye a Antonio Cordón, que le permita al Sevilla no sufrir. El sevillano hizo una limpia en el vestuario liberando de paso fichas elevadas y firmó siguiendo una ajustada ruta financiera que exige seguir generando margen en los próximos mercados para sostener el proyecto. Cuatro victorias, un empate y dos derrotas, estas últimas ante el Atlético de Madrid y el Barcelona, los dos equipos que han conseguido imponerse en el estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán. En ambas ocasiones el conjunto nervionense dio la cara y dejó tramos donde supo competir. La entrega no se negocia y el Sevilla ha conseguido enganchar a la afición. Más de 40.000 ocuparon las gradas del estadio blanquirrojo frente a los de Hansi Flick. El Sevilla ha recibido nueve goles en siete jornadas, aunque seis llegaron en las derrotas contra Atlético y Barcelona, tres en cada partidos. En los otros cinco partidos encajó solo tres, concretamente frente al Rayo, el Athletic y el Espanyol, ganando los dos primeros y empatando el tercero. Juan Iglesias relanzó al equipo con un gol frente al Valencia la jornada siguiente y en la visita a La Coruña, Miguel Sierra terminó con la condición de invicto del Dépor. Tras caer ante el intratable Barcelona en el choque previo al parón, al Sevilla le esperan dos salidas consecutivas para enfrentarse al Levante y al Real Madrid. Es la seña de identidad de este Sevilla de García Plaza, la presión adelantada independientemente del rival que tenga enfrente. Los blanquirrojos están entre los equipos de las cinco grandes ligas europeas que más recuperaciones consigue en zonas comprometidas y que más presiones realiza. El fichaje de Juan Iglesias le ha dado solidez a la defensa y Kike Salas rinde a un nivel sobresaliente, sin dejar de lado la capacidad que tiene el técnico a la hora de leer los partidos. El Sevilla ha demostrado que puede competir y ganar, pero todavía no ha demostrado que pueda controlar 90 minutos contra un rival superior. Sabe sufrir, pero también es necesario tener un fondo de armario con la calidad suficiente para realizar cambios sin que el equipo se resienta. El gol también merece un capítulo. El conjunto nervionense lleva diez tantos repartidos entre nueve futbolistas distintos. La batalla por el '9', de momento, la gana Stassin. Robbie Ure no se ha estrenado todavía. El equipo ha empezado con un notable alto. Los blanquirrojos se han marchado al parón en la quinta posición, una plaza europea que recuerda a tiempos pasados, con 13 puntos de 21 posibles. La nota en este inicio de temporada: 8,5. Fofana. El centrocampista francés fue la bomba del último día del mercado, una jugada maestra del club que consiguió convencer al Milan y al futbolista para jugar a préstamo en Nervión. Youssouf Fofana ha caído de pie en Nervión. En sus primeros cuatro partidos como sevillista registra un gol frente al Barcelona, tres titularidades y tiene la virtud de hacer mejores a sus compañeros en la mitad de la cancha. Un jugador diferencial. Entre que no termina de engancharse y que se lesiona con frecuencia, Rubén Vargas no tiene continuidad y no se sabe a ciencia cierta cuándo volverá a estar disponible para García Plaza. El técnico le espera tras el parón, pero va con cautela. Fue una de las salidas que más se daban por hechas el pasado verano, pero el Olympiacos no alcanzó las pretensiones económicas del Sevilla. Ahora toca recuperarle y volver a colocarle en el escaparate.

articles.title: OTD: (3/10/1931) A Sunderland Debut For Charlie Thomson
articles.summary: A league and FA Cup winner, Glasgow native Thomson was a red and white mainstay during the 1930s, writes John Wilson.
articles.body:
There have been two players names 'Charles Thomson' that've played for this club.

Both were greats in their own right. Both won a league championship medal, played in an FA Cup final and made over 260 appearances for the Black Cats, and both were Scottish half backs that represented their country.

There are amazing similarities between the two C. Thomsons, but this piece is about Charles Morgan Thomson, who played over twenty years after his namesake.

Born in Pollokshields, Glasgow, on 11 December 1910, Thomson was the son of a local painter and decorator. And in terms of football, it also began there, as he played for his local Pollokshields football team, from where he was scouted and joined the Roker Park squad in 1931, at the age of twenty.

Thomson was mainly an attacking right half, slight and fast, at 5 feet 8 inches and weighing 10st 6 lbs in old money. He made his debut for the club on this day in 1931, during a 2-2 draw against Blackburn Rovers at Roker Park in front of over 20,000 people, although he wouldn't become a regular in the side until the following season.

His playing style was once described by a commentator thus…

Here is a master craftsman who plays with his head as well as his feet. He sees an opening, and generally puts the ball where it is most wanted, is dainty, but surprises by the strength of his tackle.

From the turn of the year in 1934 until the outbreak of the Second World War, he hardly missed a single game for Sunderland, racking up 264 appearances in all competitions and scoring eight goals. But his two standout glories were winning the Division One championship in the 1935/1936 season and winning the FA Cup the following season in 1937.

When I look through the history books, it never ceases to amaze me just how much more inviting and attractive cup games were in those days compared to the league.

During the first cup-winning season, the league average was just under 30,000. For the cup run, it was over 50,000 and the year Charlie won his league title medal in 1936, the average gate was still only around 30,000.

Two weeks after winning the FA Cup with The Lads, he was awarded his one and only Scottish cap, when he represented his country in a 3-1 home win against Czechoslovakia.

Charlie was around during some of the most successful periods in our history, amongst some of the giants of our famous past. His team mates included Raich Carter, Sandy McNab, Bobby Gurney, Jimmy Thorpe, Johnny Mapson and Alec Hastings.

We've experienced success recently, reaching the Premier League and getting into the Europa League, but can you imagine the fan reaction at the time after winning the league and then the FA Cup the following year?

Like many around that time, the war affected their careers in more ways than one and Thomson played his last match at Anfield in 1939, before the fixture list was abandoned, and he retired far too early in 1940, aged only 29.

After the football, you could say things went full circle for Charlie, as he returned to the family business by becoming a painter, but in his case, in the shipyards on the Wear.

That was his life until his retirement, when he settled with his wife Frances, in Sherburn, County Durham. They had no children and he died aged 73 in 1984. Frances survived him by over two decades, eventually passing away in County Durham at the age of 93 in 2005.

When you see a timeline like that, starting in 1910, and ultimately ending with his wife in 2005, it shrinks time somewhat. It also helps us to better grasp the fact that these heroes don't belong to ancient history — their time flows into the club we have today.

articles.title: Fourth-quarter rally gives No. 7 Staples dramatic win over No. 6 Cheshire
articles.summary: Staples rallied from a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter against Cheshire and remained unbeaten.
articles.body:
WESTPORT - Noah Sandrew was delivered the football on a shovel pass with Staples 23 yards from the goal line and one clear thought ran through his head.

"It" happened to be the game-winning touchdown on a dramatic dive to the pylon with 5:39 remaining, when No.7-ranked Staples rallied for a 14-10 victory over No. 6 Cheshire in a wild Connecticut High School Football Alliance game Friday night in Westport.

The Rams (3-1) had built a 10-point lead by dominating the first half time of possession behind their run game and defense, but the Wreckers (4-0) turned the tables with a pair of fourth-quarter touchdowns.

Sandrew said Staples' motto is "Gotta have it," and the rally epitomized that attitude.

"Those plays out there that the team was making, we have to have them to win," Sandrew said. "Throughout the whole second half, we knew what it took to win."

Sandrew and quarterback Grant Bozeman were the big guns in the Staples' offense, with Sandrew getting 99 total yards and eight receptions, and Bozeman passing for 173 yards, 134 in the second half and two touchdowns.

The Rams and Wreckers had only played twice in the past 40 years with with Cheshire winning both times, first a 28-21 OT win in the 2009 Class LL final and then a 42-14 victory during the 2021 regular season.

That's the history, but in the moment, the Wreckers managed to flip the game story after halftime.

In the second half, the defense held the Rams in check, ending three drives with punts and another with an interception by Finn Edwards. Cheshire threatened in the final minutes, moving the ball to the Wreckers' 41-yard line, but eventually turned the ball over on downs with 46 seconds to go.

"We made all the mistakes we could make (in the first half) but it was still a 10-0 game," Staples' senior Parker Toohey said. "We came out, we executed schematically and we just played violently and we got it done."

Cheshire had already won two close games this season, defeating West Haven by two and Glastonbury by one, but suffered its first loss this time.

"We executed (in the first half), we did some good things," Cheshire coach Don Drust said. "But you've got to come out in the second half and maintain it. You've got to play for 48 minutes, not 24."

The Rams' running attack was on point in the first half, with Michael Chopak, Noel Martinez and Oliver Donroe combining for more than 160 rushing yards.

Martinez scored the game's first points on a 30-yard run and kicker Tim Reinhard added a 44-yard field goal for a 10-0 lead at halftime.

Staples, which managed just 58 yards of offense in the first half, had a strong opening drive in the second half end with a missed field goal.

The Wreckers' next drive covered 71 yards and ended with a 15-yard touchdown pass from Bozeman to Lucas Kuliga on the first play of the fourth quarter.

After the teams traded possessions, Staples took the lead on Sandrews' 23-yard touchdown on a dive.

The Wreckers defense did the rest and pitched a second-half shutout

"We showed it getting the ball and wearing them down over the game," Toohey said. "I think our identity has been our defense in the past couple of years. Last year, we weren't up to our standard so this year we worked hard in the weight room, we came back, and we're better than ever."

The junior receiver had a big night with eight receptions and 99 total yards while also scoring the game-winning touchdown on a dive into the end zone.

"Our guys care so deeply and they're so passionate about our program and each other and wanting to fight side-by-side. We knew (Cheshire) was trying to possess but we felt confident that over the course of the game, we were going to be able to hit our shots and cash in on some big opportunities." - Staples coach Matty Jacowleff

articles.title: Jean-Philippe Mateta: United target makes key decision on future
articles.summary: Manchester United are preparing to reinforce the squad in 2027 after an underwhelming start to the new season. The Red Devils are 12th in the Premier League...
articles.body:
Manchester United are preparing to reinforce the squad in 2027 after an underwhelming start to the new season. The Red Devils are 12th in the Premier League table after five games, having managed just one win in the league so far.

They have, however, enjoyed a blockbuster return to the Champions League, securing a 4-0 win over Sabah in the first league stage game last month. Unfortunately, Michael Carrick's team was also knocked out of the EFL Cup by Brighton & Hove Albion in the third round.

The situation has piled pressure on the English manager, who was handed the full-time job at the end of last season after helping United finish third in the league. Despite revamping the midfield over the summer, Carrick's start to the new campaign has left a lot to be desired.

The Red Devils' lack of precision in front of goal has also prompted talk of possible attacking additions in January. A new striker could help share the load with Benjamin Sesko and Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta has been mentioned as a possible option.

A recent report relayed by The Peoples Person states that the Frenchman's camp has already contacted United about the possibility of a move in 2027. However, there remained the possibility of Palace convincing him to sign a new deal, and an update on that situation has now emerged which will delight United fans.

According to Football Insider , Mateta will not sign a new deal with Palace. The report states: "Jean-Philippe Mateta will leave Crystal Palace in 2027 and will not put pen to paper on a new contract, sources have told Football Insider."

"The only question mark surrounding the 29-year-old's future is now whether he will leave in January or upon the expiry of his contract at the end of the season."

"A number of clubs in the Premier League and across Europe have been keeping a close eye on his situation, and the Eagles could open the door to offers in January."

Jean-Philippe Mateta Stats: 2025/26 Season

Palace could allow Mateta to run down his contract

The report goes on to add that Palace are also ready to let the Frenchman leave for free next summer, as they want him to continue leading the line for this season. It states: "The Eagles are also content to allow the striker to run down his contract and leave on a free next summer, in exchange for another year of him leading the line."

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, journalist Pete O'Rourke also insisted that Mateta is certain to leave in 2027. He said: "His future is pretty much certain at Palace right now, he's in the final year of his contract and we do expect him to leave Palace."

"The question is about whether that's in January or next summer when his contract expires, that's the decision Crystal Palace have to make."

Mateta could bring a physical presence to United's attack, something they desperately lack at the moment. If there is an opportunity to sign the Frenchman in January for a nominal fee, the Red Devils should grab it with both hands rather than wait for the summer.

✅ Previous reports relayed by TPP suggest that Mateta could leave in 2027.⚠️ The player is yet to confirm that he will not sign an extension.

TPP view We believe it is increasingly likely that Mateta will leave Palace in 2027, however, it is too soon to speculate on whether a final decision on the matter has already been reached.

articles.title: England XI vs Croatia – Predicted lineup and team news
articles.summary: England will press on with their UEFA Nations League campaign this Saturday as they travel to face Croatia at Stadion HNK Rijeka in an away fixture.Under Tho...
articles.body:
England will press on with their UEFA Nations League campaign this Saturday as they travel to face Croatia at Stadion HNK Rijeka in an away fixture.

Under Thomas Tuchel, England have been building positive momentum, securing three wins from their last five games across all competitions. After a tight 3-2 defeat to Spain in their opening Nations League match, the Three Lions responded impressively with a 2-0 away win against Czechia in their most recent outing. England also go into this game with confidence from their head-to-head record, having beaten Croatia 4-2 at the 2026 World Cup just a few months earlier.

Thomas Tuchel has confirmed that his 24-man travelling squad is fully fit ahead of the match in Rijeka, although several established first-team players are not part of this group.

Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford is expected to return to the starting lineup, replacing James Trafford as part of a planned rotation policy. In defence, Ezri Konsa has recovered from a minor knock, trained without problems on Friday, and is now the leading candidate to start alongside Marc Guéhi in the centre of defence.

England have had to manage some late changes to their squad. Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly has left the camp and will not be available for this fixture.

The team is also without a number of high-profile absentees who pulled out before the international window: Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, and Marcus Rashford. Even with these missing names, Tuchel still has a powerful attacking unit at his disposal, headlined by Harry Kane and supported by Jude Bellingham and Bukayo Saka.

Possible England starting XI: Pickford; Trent, Chalobah, Guehi, Hall; Anderson, Garner; Saka, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane

The match will kick off at 5pm BST on Saturday, 3rd October.

For viewers in the United Kingdom, the Croatia vs England Nations League match will be shown live and free of charge on ITV1.

articles.body:
Spain will welcome Czechia to the Estadio Municipal Carlos Tartiere in Oviedo this Saturday for their latest UEFA Nations League Group 3 fixture, aiming to keep their remarkable winning run alive.

Under Luis de la Fuente, Spain are in extraordinary shape and currently unbeaten in 40 consecutive matches—a record-breaking sequence that includes major tournament success. La Roja have won nine games in a row across all competitions, a streak that features their World Cup final victory over Argentina, secured by a 1-0 win. That momentum has carried straight into the Nations League, where they sit atop Group 3 after a 3-2 away win against England at Wembley and a commanding 4-1 home victory over Croatia in Seville.

Despite leading the group following the 4-1 defeat of Croatia, de la Fuente is dealing with a string of absences that have disrupted his plans.

Left-back Alejandro Grimaldo has left the camp with a thigh problem and has been replaced by Real Madrid's Fran García. The attack has been hit hard: Nico Williams is out with a thigh issue, and Ferran Torres has withdrawn because of ankle discomfort.

Defender Eric García also departed early due to a knee complaint, leading to Robin Le Normand being recalled to the squad. In response to these setbacks, 20-year-old Real Madrid forward Carlos Espí has received his first senior call-up to bolster the attacking options.

Key midfield figures Rodri, Pedri and Dani Olmo are all fully rested and working their way back into contention, so they are expected to be managed carefully rather than thrown straight into the starting XI.

Possible Spain starting XI: Simon; Pubill, Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Ruiz, Rodri; Yamal, Olmo, N Williams; Oyarzabal
