articles.body:
Scotland and North Macedonia face each other in the third group fixture of their UEFA Nations League campaign on Saturday at the Nacionalna Arena Tose Proeska as both teams look for their first win in this international break.

North Macedonia vs Scotland – Match preview and team news

Venue: Nacionalna Arena Tose Proeska, Skopje.

North Macedonia deals with its own set of fitness setbacks ahead of tonight's clash at the Todor Proeski National Arena.

The hosts will be missing experienced left-back Ezgjan Alioski, who was forced to withdraw from the squad after sustaining a painful calf injury in their previous outing against Switzerland.

Midfielder Boban Nikolov has also been ruled out of the camp due to fitness issues, narrowing the team's options in central areas. Despite these absences, the Lions boast plenty of star power in the final third.

Inspirational captain Enis Bardhi is poised to earn his 84th international cap, pulling the strings as the primary creative force in midfield.

He will be closely supported by RB Leipzig's Eljif Elmas in an advanced role, while Rangers forward Bojan Miovski is fully expected to lead the attacking line up front.

Scotland enters this crucial fixture facing significant selection headaches, particularly in defence. Centre-back Jack Hendry is suspended after picking up an early red card against Switzerland, forcing manager Sebastien Pocognoli to reshuffle his backline.

The squad was already heavily depleted prior to the international window, with key figures like Kieran Tierney, Kenny McLean, Scott McTominay, Lawrence Shankland, and Che Adams all ruled out due to ongoing injuries or unavailability.

To fill the defensive void, Swansea City's Stephen Welsh or Luis Binks is widely expected to step into the back three alongside veteran Scott McKenna.

On a brighter note, captain Andy Robertson is set to earn his historic 100th international cap from the left flank, moving closer to the all-time record. He will link up with Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson, who are tipped to anchor the midfield.

North Macedonia finds itself in a historic slump, having gone six consecutive matches without scoring a goal. They currently sit at the bottom of Group E after losing both opening Nations League fixtures without a reply. Goce Sedloski's side suffered a heavy 3-0 loss at home to Switzerland, followed by a disappointing 2-0 defeat away against Slovenia, leaving them desperate to break their dry spell tonight.

Scotland enters this contest searching for an attacking spark under Sebastien Pocognoli, having failed to score in their last four matches across all competitions. They opened their UEFA Nations League campaign with a hard-fought 0-0 draw away to Slovenia, but followed it with a bruising 3-0 home defeat against Switzerland after an early red card. However, their formidable away record of losing only once in their last seven travels provides strong confidence.

North Macedonia: Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Zajkov, Musliu, Alomerovic; Atanasov, Gashtarov; Mitrovski, Bardhi, Elmas; Miovski

Scotland: Gunn; Binks, McKenna, Welsh; Hickey, Gilmour, Ferguson, McGinn, Robertson; Bowie, McBurnie

How to watch North Macedonia vs Scotland?

The match will be broadcast live on BBC Two and BBC Scotland.

Spain will host Czechia in their next UEFA Nations League fixture on Saturday at the Estadio Municipal Carlos Tartiere in Oviedo as they continue their winning streak.

Spain vs Czechia – Match preview and team news

Venue: Estadio Municipal Carlos Tartiere, Oviedo.

Spain enters this fixture leading Group 3 following a convincing victory over Croatia, but manager Luis de la Fuente faces significant squad disruptions due to a wave of injuries.

Left-back Alejandro Grimaldo was forced to withdraw from the camp due to a thigh injury and has been replaced by Real Madrid's Fran García.

The attacking line takes a massive hit as both Nico Williams and Ferran Torres have withdrawn from the squad due to thigh and ankle issues, respectively.

Additionally, Eric García left the camp early with a knee injury, prompting a recall for Robin Le Normand. In a surprise squad addition, 20-year-old Real Madrid forward Carlos Espí has earned his first senior call-up to cover the attacking shortages.

De la Fuente is expected to heavily rotate his starting lineup, with key midfielders Rodri, Pedri, and Dani Olmo all fully rested and pushing to return to action.

The visitors will be heavily short-handed in midfield as Pavel Šulc serves a suspension following a direct red card picked up in the first half against England.

Further complicating Denia's plans, midfielder Adam Karabec is highly doubtful for this clash after limping off injured during the previous match.

Experienced right-back Vladimír Coufal also remains an injury doubt after missing the England fixture entirely with a knock. On a positive note, Czechia could hand an international debut to 23-year-old Rangers forward Ryan Naderi, who recently committed his international future to the country over Germany. Denia will likely look to Adam Hložek and Alex Král to provide leadership and stability to a depleted side.

Spain enters this contest in spectacular, unbeatable form under Luis de la Fuente, riding an incredible 40-match unbeaten streak. La Roja has secured nine consecutive victories, including their historic World Cup triumph where they defeated Argentina 1-0 in the final. They have perfectly carried that momentum into the UEFA Nations League, topping Group 3 after defeating England 3-2 at Wembley followed by a dominant 4-1 thrashing of Croatia in Seville.

Czechia is enduring a highly challenging run under manager Santi Denia, managing just one draw and four losses in their last five fixtures. Following a difficult summer World Cup campaign where they finished bottom of Group A with a single point, their struggles have rolled into the Nations League. They sit last in the group without a point, following back-to-back defeats—a 2-1 loss to Croatia and a recent 2-0 home loss to England.

Czechia: Kovar; Chaloupek, Hranac, Krejci, Slama; Sadliek, Cerv; Radosta, Kral, Lingr; Hlozek
